accepted.s: What proportion of the elderly is reported to be living in nuclear households?
accepted.x: Over 55% of the elderly are reported to live in nuclear households.
accepted.tq: Use the precise percentage rather than a nearby rounded figure.
accepted.sec: Ageing and family - old age homes, intergenerational support, living alone, rural vs urban

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding family support for the elderly:
1. Care inside the joint family is weakening.
2. More than half of the elderly now live in nuclear households.
3. The weakening of joint-family care is associated with the growing importance of living arrangements outside the traditional joint family.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Care within joint families is weakening, while over 55% of the elderly live in nuclear households, highlighting changing family support arrangements.
accepted.tq: Link the demographic figure with its stated social consequence.
accepted.sec: Ageing and family - old age homes, intergenerational support, living alone, rural vs urban

accepted.s: Under which programme can NGOs receive support of up to 90% of the cost of old age homes?
o: National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly
accepted.x: The Integrated Programme for Older Persons provides NGOs with support of up to 90% of the costs of old age homes.
accepted.tq: Match the welfare intervention with the exact programme responsible for it.
accepted.sec: Ageing and family - old age homes, intergenerational support, living alone, rural vs urban

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position associated with NPSC 2011?
o: It supported ageing in place and drew attention to destitution among rural elderly persons.
It restricted elderly welfare exclusively to persons living in joint families.
It recommended abolishing NGO support for old age homes.
It favoured institutionalisation of all elderly persons in urban old age homes.
accepted.x: NPSC 2011 backed the concept of ‘ageing in place’ and highlighted destitution among the rural elderly.
accepted.tq: Distinguish community-based ageing support from compulsory institutional care.
accepted.sec: Ageing and family - old age homes, intergenerational support, living alone, rural vs urban

accepted.s: Which State is the first in India to have a Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department, a Commission and an Elderly Budget?
accepted.x: Kerala is the first State to establish all three: a Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department, a Commission and an Elderly Budget.
accepted.tq: Identify the State associated with the complete institutional framework for senior citizens.
accepted.sec: Ageing and family - old age homes, intergenerational support, living alone, rural vs urban

accepted.s: The draft Population Management Policy of Andhra Pradesh represents a shift from which approach to which approach?
o: From population control to population management
From population management to population control
From ageing management to migration control
From rural development to urban planning
accepted.x: The draft policy marks an Andhra Pradesh shift from population control towards population management.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of policy change by separating control from management.
accepted.sec: Population control debates - two-child norms, AP stance, dependency ratio

accepted.s:
With reference to the draft Population Management Policy of Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. It offers ₹25,000 for a second or third child.
2. It removes the two-child norm for local elections.
3. It is based on five pillars.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The draft policy provides the stated incentive, removes the two-child norm for local elections and rests on five pillars.
accepted.tq: Check several features of one policy before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Population control debates - two-child norms, AP stance, dependency ratio

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five pillars of the draft Population Management Policy of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Matrutva, Shakti, Kshema, Naipunyam and Sanjeevani are the five pillars. Samriddhi is not included in the stated list.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in an otherwise familiar list.
accepted.sec: Population control debates - two-child norms, AP stance, dependency ratio

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the legal position in Javed v. State of Haryana (2003)?
o: The Supreme Court struck down Haryana’s two-child norm as unconstitutional.
The case abolished two-child norms for local elections throughout India.
The Supreme Court upheld Haryana’s two-child norm.
The case concerned only the calculation of the dependency ratio.
accepted.x: In Javed v. State of Haryana (2003), the Supreme Court upheld Haryana’s two-child norm.
accepted.tq: Use the case name and year to identify the precise judicial outcome.
accepted.sec: Population control debates - two-child norms, AP stance, dependency ratio

accepted.s: The dependency ratio is calculated by which of the following formulas?
accepted.x: The dependency ratio is calculated as the population aged 0–14 plus the population aged 65 and above, divided by the population aged 15–64.
accepted.tq: Separate the dependent-age groups in the numerator from the working-age denominator.
accepted.sec: Population control debates - two-child norms, AP stance, dependency ratio

accepted.s: According to SRS 2024, which of the following correctly represents the shares of the working-age population and children, respectively?
accepted.x: SRS 2024 gives the working-age population share as 66.4% and the children’s share as 24%.
accepted.tq: Read the paired percentages in the order asked.
accepted.sec: Population control debates - two-child norms, AP stance, dependency ratio

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding recent demographic indicators and ageing trends?
1. India’s total fertility rate in SRS 2024 is 1.9.
2. The RBI identifies Kerala and Tamil Nadu as ageing States by 2036.
3. Kerala and Tamil Nadu are identified as ageing States because their dependency ratio is stated to be zero.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The SRS 2024 total fertility rate is 1.9, and the RBI refers to Kerala and Tamil Nadu as ageing States by 2036; no zero dependency ratio is stated.
accepted.tq: Reject an invented extreme explanation while retaining the two stated demographic facts.

accepted.s: The draft Population Management Policy referred to in relation to Andhra Pradesh was introduced in which month and year?
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh draft Population Management Policy was introduced in March 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the policy’s date to distinguish it from other current demographic developments.

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh’s population is given as approximately 495.77 lakh. This represents what share of India’s population and what rank?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh’s population is stated as 495.77 lakh, accounting for 4.09% of India’s population and placing it 10th.
accepted.tq: Treat the population figure, percentage and rank as a linked numerical set.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Introduction of India’s first national family planning programme
B. Judgment in Javed v. State of Haryana
C. Draft Population Management Policy of Andhra Pradesh
D. SRS 2024 total fertility rate reference
accepted.x: India launched its first national family planning programme in 1952, Javed v. State of Haryana was decided in 2003, SRS 2024 provides the fertility-rate reference, and the Andhra Pradesh draft policy dates to March 2026.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest landmark first, then place the 2003, 2024 and 2026 developments.

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

List-I                  List-II
A. India                 1. First Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department
B. Kerala                2. First national family planning programme
C. Andhra Pradesh       3. Draft Population Management Policy

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: India introduced the first national family planning programme in 1952, Kerala was first with the senior-citizens institutional framework, and Andhra Pradesh is associated with the draft Population Management Policy.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair India–first national family planning programme and eliminate the codes.
